outputs.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Ansible managed
# Applies hdparm_tune settings at boot. Ubuntu's udev hook
# (/lib/udev/hdparm -> 95hdparm-apm) skips -B and -S for disks whose udev
# properties lack ID_ATA_FEATURE_SET_APM=1, so /etc/hdparm.conf alone does not
# survive a reboot on those disks.
set -u

wait_sec=60
rc=0

apply() {
  local dev="$1"
  shift
  local waited=0
  while [[ ! -b "${dev}" && "${waited}" -lt "${wait_sec}" ]]; do
    sleep 1
    waited=$((waited + 1))
  done
  if [[ ! -b "${dev}" ]]; then
    echo "hdparm-tune: ${dev} not found after ${wait_sec}s" >&2
    rc=1
    return
  fi
  if hdparm "$@" "${dev}" >/dev/null; then
    echo "hdparm-tune: applied $* to ${dev}"
  else
    echo "hdparm-tune: hdparm $* failed for ${dev}" >&2
    rc=1
  fi
}

apply /dev/disk/by-id/owned-a -B 127 -S 241
apply /dev/disk/by-id/owned-b -B 127 -M 128 -S 241
apply /dev/disk/by-id/owned-c -S 0
exit "${rc}"
outputs.unit:
# Ansible managed
[Unit]
Description=Apply hdparm_tune disk settings (APM, acoustic management, spindown)
After=local-fs.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
RemainAfterExit=yes
ExecStart=/usr/local/sbin/hdparm-tune-apply

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
